case.message: Did Tesla stay within its stated 2023 and 2024 capital-spending outlook? Give the quoted ranges, actual cash PP&E spending, and compare revenue and net income with GM and Ford.

data.response:
# Tesla Capital-Spending Outlook and Peer Comparison

**Contradicted**

TSLA revenue for the fiscal period ended 2024-12-31 was $97.690 billion [E06fb99d6f5](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828025003063/0001628280-25-003063-index.html), up from $96.773 billion for 2023-12-31 [E11b4f42020](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828024002390/0001628280-24-002390-index.html). TSLA net income for the fiscal period ended 2024-12-31 was $7.091 billion [E882dff63b5](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828025003063/0001628280-25-003063-index.html), down from $14.997 billion for 2023-12-31 [E67dab066ab](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828024002390/0001628280-24-002390-index.html). TSLA cash PP&E purchases for the fiscal period ended 2024-12-31 was $11.339 billion [Efe9447dc7f](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828025003063/0001628280-25-003063-index.html), up from $8.898 billion for 2023-12-31 [Ec516a365d5](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828024002390/0001628280-24-002390-index.html). The retrieved outlook gave a capital-spending range of $6.000 billion to $8.000 billion for the year ending 2023-12-31 [E730dbabced](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000095017023001409/tsla-20221231.htm). Reported cash PP&E purchases were $8.898 billion, above quoted range [Ec516a365d5](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828024002390/0001628280-24-002390-index.html). The retrieved outlook gave a capital-spending range of $7.000 billion to $9.000 billion for the year ending 2024-12-31 [E730dbabced](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000095017023001409/tsla-20221231.htm). Reported cash PP&E purchases were $11.339 billion, above quoted range [Efe9447dc7f](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828025003063/0001628280-25-003063-index.html).

## What was knowable then

As of its 2022 Form 10-K filed on January 31, 2023, Tesla stated that it expected capital expenditures to be between $6.00 and $8.00 billion in 2023 and between $7.00 and $9.00 billion in each of the following two fiscal years [E730dbabced](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000095017023001409/tsla-20221231.htm). Management noted that these expectations were subject to varying levels of inflation, project pipelines, and infrastructure growth [E309c4ed784](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000095017023001409/tsla-20221231.htm). Previously, Tesla had reported capital expenditures of $7.158 billion for fiscal year 2022, which fell within its prior expected range of $6.00 to $8.00 billion [E47389143dc](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000095017023001409/0000950170-23-001409-index.html) [E48a453ba97](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000095017022019867/tsla-20220930.htm).

## What happened later

For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, Tesla reported actual cash payments for property, plant, and equipment of $8.898 billion, which exceeded the quoted upper bound of $8.00 billion [Ec516a365d5](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828024002390/0001628280-24-002390-index.html). For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, actual cash capex rose to $11.339 billion, exceeding the quoted upper bound of $9.00 billion [Efe9447dc7f](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828025003063/0001628280-25-003063-index.html). Tesla's annual net income shifted from $14.997 billion in 2023 to $7.091 billion in 2024 [E67dab066ab](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828024002390/0001628280-24-002390-index.html) [E882dff63b5](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828025003063/0001628280-25-003063-index.html).

## The peer test

For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, Tesla reported revenue of $96.773 billion and net income of $14.997 billion [E11b4f42020](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828024002390/0001628280-24-002390-index.html) [E67dab066ab](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828024002390/0001628280-24-002390-index.html), General Motors reported revenue of $171.842 billion and net income of $10.127 billion [E05a1eabc58](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1467858/000146785824000031/0001467858-24-000031-index.html) [Eb2e7c6d470](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1467858/000146785824000031/0001467858-24-000031-index.html), and Ford reported revenue of $176.191 billion and net income of $4.347 billion [E72a491f2a6](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/37996/000003799624000009/0000037996-24-000009-index.html) [E90b162746e](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/37996/000003799624000009/0000037996-24-000009-index.html). For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, Tesla reported revenue of $97.690 billion and net income of $7.091 billion [E06fb99d6f5](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828025003063/0001628280-25-003063-index.html) [E882dff63b5](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828025003063/0001628280-25-003063-index.html), General Motors reported revenue of $187.442 billion and net income of $6.008 billion [E16ec1705e6](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1467858/000146785825000032/0001467858-25-000032-index.html) [E1352fe29f3](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1467858/000146785825000032/0001467858-25-000032-index.html), and Ford reported revenue of $184.992 billion and net income of $5.879 billion [E7a1d3a94d0](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/37996/000003799625000013/0000037996-25-000013-index.html) [Ebebae703eb](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/37996/000003799625000013/0000037996-25-000013-index.html).

## Cross-examination

The reported capital expenditures of $8.898 billion in 2023 and $11.339 billion in 2024 are verified management outcomes that can be directly compared against the numeric thresholds provided in the 2022 Form 10-K outlook statement [E730dbabced](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000095017023001409/tsla-20221231.htm) [Ec516a365d5](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828024002390/0001628280-24-002390-index.html) [Efe9447dc7f](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828025003063/0001628280-25-003063-index.html). Although management highlighted qualitative factors such as inflation and project pipelines, the quantitative outcomes exceeded the published boundaries [E309c4ed784](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000095017023001409/tsla-20221231.htm). Revenue expansion and positive operating cash flows do not independently verify specific capital spending targets or validate unstated funding sources [Eb3b11f8745](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828024002390/0001628280-24-002390-index.html).

## Limits

- No annual USD capex observation under supported XBRL tags was available for Ford, preventing direct capex peer comparison for that entity.
- Macroeconomic series and stock prices are drawn from unadjusted or revised hindsight contexts.

For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, Tesla reported revenue of $97.690 billion and net income of $7.091 billion [E06fb99d6f5] [E882dff63b5], General Motors reported revenue of $187.442 billion and net income of $6.008 billion [E16ec1705e6] [E1352fe29f3], and Ford reported revenue of $184.992 billion and net income of $5.879 billion [E7a1d3a94d0] [Ebebae703eb].

sections.title: Cross-examination
sections.text: The reported capital expenditures of $8.898 billion in 2023 and $11.339 billion in 2024 are verified management outcomes that can be directly compared against the numeric thresholds provided in the 2022 Form 10-K outlook statement [E730dbabced] [Ec516a365d5] [Efe9447dc7f]. Although management highlighted qualitative factors such as inflation and project pipelines, the quantitative outcomes exceeded the published boundaries [E309c4ed784]. Revenue expansion and positive operating cash flows do not independently verify specific capital spending targets or validate unstated funding sources [Eb3b11f8745].
